Champion Leccy browse by type volume/amplification amplification preamp / clean boost browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by type pitch/octave octaver octave fuzz octave fuzz (1 octave down) browse by type sound source oscillator browse by enclosure pedal Champion Leccy The Evil Twin Published on April 12, 2017 Champion Leccy boost / preamp distortion octave fuzz (1 octave down) oscillator random controlled pedal 2025 edition (another 25 pedals made) 2025 edition Information Champion Leccy The Evil Twin is a very versatile boost pedal. It is a combination of two Wee Fettle Boosts and a whole bunch of craziness all in one box. The first foot switch operates a standard Wee Fettle Boost giving its usual characteristic dirty JFET boost. The second foot switch engages its Evil Twin with a bunch of extra switches to control the amount of evil you want to add. Options include lo-fi poor tracking lower octave randomness, frequency dependent resonance, a tremolo-like effect and oscillations. The oscillations can be controlled by all the controls on the pedal as well as the guitar's volume knob and pickup selector switch, turning your guitar into a whole different instrument. The controls are highly interactive. Controls are: Foot switch 1 gain knob boost switch Foot switch 2 gain knob volume knob 3 switches for shaping the craziness The top switch in central position is the stock boost circuit. To the left it adds lo-fi pitch glitchiness, in this setting you can also use the second switch (depending on the gain and volume settings). With the switch to the right, all the controls come into effect shaping the rate of the tremolo effect (if set right), or the pitch and character of the oscillations. All Evil Twin pedals are hand-painted. The artwork revolves around the theme of two rather unique Champion Leccy characters. - **Archive parent:** Evil Twin
- **Builder:** Champion Leccy
- **Catalog type:** Boost / Distortion / Fuzz / Oscillator
- **Identity:** Two-Fettle-Boost-derived design with one side retaining boost function and the other adding octave, resonance, tremolo-like and oscillator behavior. [1][2]

- Two Fettle Boost-derived sections.
- Fettle lineage uses a **JFET** gain stage plus BJT-based later gain stage. [1]
- The “evil” section adds lower-octave/randomized behavior, resonance and oscillation controls. [1][2]

- JFET/BJT architecture inherited from the Fettle family.
- Exact transistor part numbers are not established.

- Exact clipping-device part numbers are not established.

- Two Fettle-derived channels.
- Second channel adds the unusual oscillator/sub-octave/resonance functionality. [1]

Champion Leccy documented:
- Improved power section.
- One former internal trim moved to an external potentiometer.
- Portrait-format enclosure instead of the earlier landscape layout.
- New artwork.
- Core behavior retained. [2]

This is a documented hardware/layout update, not merely a finish change.

- Model-specific current draw is not securely preserved in the reviewed sources.

The standard side supplies dirty JFET boost while the Evil side adds sub-octave randomness, resonance, tremolo-like modulation and oscillation. Champion Leccy notes that the oscillation can interact with the pedal controls and guitar settings. [1][2]

- **Identity:** High
- **Fettle lineage:** High
- **2025 hardware update:** High
- **Oscillator/sub-octave architecture:** High
- **Exact devices:** Unknown

Cart news and updates Summer Leccy – 2025: May you live in interesting times Posted by Woolly on June 11, 2025 Yes, I know we’re already well into June. The article just took a bit longer than planned and I couldn’t think of a clever title for this month, and anyway, I started this article in April, so on balance its cosmic centre is still somewhere in May technically. If you wanted to jump all the rambling for something a bit more exciting and pedally, head to the heading What’s coming next! ahead (below). Since the last article in February I’ve been working on getting Champion Leccy back on its feet. It has been a bit up and down, but things are looking canny. The back pain is manageable. It’ll be an ongoing challenge, but I’m confident about the future. So that’s a nice positive start. It’s still taking a bit of experimentation to find a good balanced routine, but I’ve been keeping decent pace with the plans and expectations I laid out last time. I’m able to build regularly, the store has been restocked, I have renewed enough mental energy to get back out there on instagram, sales have started to pick up again and I’m even working on some new designs! Not going to lie though, I wrote a huge article that I thought was jam-packed with revelations, then looked back at the February update article and realised that I’d already included most of it in there, it way also written way more betterly too. I have since deleted several paragraphs from this article in shame. But basically, the last few months have gone well, progress is steady, so I’m feeling good about talking about plans with more certainty. A handful of things have changed since last time, and there is some new news to report. So, here is what’s what. Where I am now This section is about what is happening now. If that’s boring please skip to the future. Building Stock I’m still currently trying to restock the store. It’s been like spinning plates, but I’m almost there. Swan Hunters keep selling out and a few things are getting low again, but everything is either in stock or returning soon (Swan Hunters returning soon!). The plan is to keep chipping away at the builds, so nothing is out of stock for long. I’ll be looking to restock retailers shortly too! Tariffs The thing no-one wants to be talking about, but that also can’t be ignored! The long and short of it is, the situation keeps changing, so it’s impossible to plan. No-one has any information they can put any faith in. Tariffs, in case you don’t know but want to know, are a tax that the importer pays. So everything costs more now. I intend to keep prices as low as possible for as long as possible. I can’t offer any predictions at this point. Fingers crossed. I’ve given up worrying about it and I’ve stopped trying to follow the news, because my nervous system prefers to not feel like it’s under attack constantly. I will deal with things as and when they happen. Again, fingers crossed. All of them. All fingers crossed. The Evil Twin It’s out there! It’s direct sales only and it’s a limited run. Unless you know what this is, you probably don’t know what this is, so, what’s the craic!? Well, in terms of what it does, it’s an early original design that oscillates and creates mayhem and is fun, but also unusably loud. Both sides are “Fettle Boosts” of some description that can be used independently. They are pretty close to the V1 Fettles. The left hand (or sinister) side has an evil switch that makes it into an oscillator (depending on the settings), at which point everything interacts. It does drones, chirping sounds, suboctave synthy nonsense, all sorts of nonsense. In fact it was this design that led to the tagline ‘Electronic Nonsense’, because of all the nonsense it enjoys.
